apiMessages.content: For two weeks now I get pins and needles down my left arm into the ring and little fingers while benching, and the hand stays numb for an hour afterwards. Add a second press day and push the weight up.

content.text:
Stop benching — that's not a loading issue. Pins and needles into the ring/little fingers with hour-long numbness is classic ulnar nerve involvement, and it's been going on two weeks. That's a nerve symptom, not soreness, and it falls under "named injury/symptom" I won't program around.

I'm not adding a second press day or increasing weight. See a clinician (sports medicine or PT) before any more bench pressing — they need to clear the nerve before loading resumes.

I'll flag this so it's not lost:
No memory tool is actually available to me here, so I can't log that to injuries.md — but I'll flag it on today's schedule instead.

Adding volume and weight on the exact movement provoking it risks turning a reversible irritation into lasting nerve damage. That's outside what I'll program around regardless of how minor it feels to you.

I'm not asking you to overhaul your life — see a doctor, PT, or even urgent care if sooner access is easier. That's the only path back to more bench volume from me.

What I can do right now: keep training everything else — legs, pull work, core — and leave bench alone until you've got clearance. Want that?
